lead.headline: CoreWeave's Blowout Quarter Revives the AI Trade as Nasdaq Jumps 1.6%
lead.deck: A 25% surge in the AI cloud provider's shares pulled chipmakers and the wider market back from Tuesday's inflation scare, lifting Europe's Stoxx 600 to a record close.
body: CoreWeave reported quarterly revenue of nearly $3.7 billion and a loss of $709 million, both better than analysts expected, and raised its full-year revenue forecast to $13.3 billion. Its chief executive called it a breakout quarter, and the company said it expects to turn a profit on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028. The shares rose about 25%.

The results eased worries that spending on AI infrastructure was running ahead of demand, and chip stocks led the rebound. Micron gained about 12%, SanDisk 14%, Marvell 9% and Intel 7.5%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF added 6%. Nvidia rose about 3% after losing 10% over the previous two sessions, as its board continues to review CEO Jensen Huang's conduct ahead of results on 17 November.

The S&P 500 climbed 98.45 points, or 1.31%, to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq Composite rose 400.31 points to 25,466.19 and the Dow added 254.60 points to 52,486.49. Apple gained 2% to a record close. The rally was narrow, however: Microsoft, Meta and Amazon all fell, and consumer cyclical stocks lagged.

The bond market was closed for Veterans Day, leaving Tuesday's inflation-driven jump in yields unresolved, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% and a December Fed rate rise still priced as close to certain. Gold slipped about 1% to roughly $3,990 an ounce. In Europe, tech shares rose 2.5% and Siemens Energy jumped nearly 11%, while Indian stocks rallied as markets reopened after Diwali.

top: CoreWeave shares surged about 25% on record results and a higher forecast, lifting the Nasdaq 1.6% and the S&P 500 1.3%.
Europe's Stoxx 600 closed at a record 663.05 as Siemens Energy jumped nearly 11% on a higher margin outlook and a much bigger dividend.
Sensex rose 773 points and the Nifty closed above 25,250 as PSU banks led India's post-Diwali rally; the rupee firmed to 93.70.
Morgan Stanley data showed equity hedge funds cut risk at the fastest pace in about a decade in early November.
easyJet shareholders approved Apollo's £5.7 billion takeover, and Polymarket confirmed job cuts as it eyes a possible 2027 listing.

items.headline: Tech Leads Wall Street Back Into the Green
items.body: AI and chip stocks drove a broad rebound after Tuesday's inflation-led sell-off, with utilities and technology the best-performing sectors. Treasury trading was closed for Veterans Day, so bonds will react to the rally today.

items.headline: European Shares Hit a Record Close
items.body: Semiconductor makers Soitec, Aixtron and Infineon rallied alongside Siemens Energy, and Germany's DAX gained about 1.2% to sit near its all-time high. Defence names fell, with Rheinmetall down nearly 7%.

items.headline: Asia Extends Its Chip-Led Recovery
items.body: Tokyo rose for a third straight session and Seoul closed near 5,375, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell about 1% to 24,315.92, the region's main laggard.

items.headline: Oil Rebounds as Iran Talks Stall
items.body: Crude recovered part of its steep November slide after Iran's top security official denied holding talks with Washington and said enriched nuclear material would not leave the country. Gold eased about 1% as money moved into stocks.

items.headline: CoreWeave Soars on a Raised Forecast
items.body: The AI data-centre operator beat revenue and loss estimates, lifted its full-year revenue outlook to $13.3 billion and set a first-half 2028 target for adjusted profitability.

items.headline: Memory and Hardware Makers Ride the Wave
items.body: Micron, SanDisk, Seagate and Western Digital posted double-digit or near-double-digit gains, while Oracle and Dell also rose sharply. Microsoft fell about 2.3% and Meta about 2%.

items.headline: Siemens Energy Rallies, Czech Defence Group Slumps
items.body: Siemens Energy raised its 2027 margin expectations and plans to more than triple its dividend. Czech ammunition maker CSG fell sharply after cutting its full-year operating margin forecast.

items.headline: Banks and Autos Power Dalal Street
items.body: Mahindra & Mahindra, InterGlobe Aviation, Trent and Tata Steel led the Nifty, while Adani Ports, ICICI Bank and HCL Technologies lagged. The Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 1.61%.

items.headline: easyJet Investors Back Apollo Buyout
items.body: About 97% of votes cast at the court meeting supported the private-equity firm's cash offer. Regulatory approvals and High Court sanction are still needed, with completion expected by the end of March 2027.

items.headline: UK Watchdog Turns Up Heat on McCormick–Unilever Food Deal
items.body: Bloomberg reported that Britain's Competition and Markets Authority is threatening a deeper phase 2 probe of McCormick's purchase of Unilever's food business unless the companies offer remedies. The deal has already cleared US antitrust review.

items.headline: Kimberly-Clark's Kenvue Deal Clears Turkey
items.body: Turkey's competition authority granted conditional approval to Kimberly-Clark's acquisition of the Tylenol maker, according to MLex, another regulatory step for the consumer-health tie-up.

items.headline: Equity Funds Make Record Retreat From Risk
items.body: Morgan Stanley's prime brokerage said global equity hedge funds cut risk at the steepest pace in more than a decade through the first week of November, the largest drop in long/short gross exposure since 2016.

items.headline: Macro and Trend Funds Suffer a Bruising Stretch
items.body: Macro and trend-following strategies are enduring one of their worst runs in years even as stocks rebound, caught out by the sharp reversal in Treasuries after Tuesday's hot inflation print.

items.headline: Ex-Goldman and Capital Group Pair Launch AI-Run Fund
items.body: Poesis, founded by former Capital Group manager Alex Popa and ex-Goldman machine-learning head Charles Elkan, will let AI agents research and trade a US equity portfolio under human risk limits. Its first strategy opens to outside investors in early 2027.

items.headline: CICC Readies China-Focused Fund of Hedge Funds
items.body: The Chinese investment bank could launch the vehicle as early as this month, pitching it to endowments and family offices.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO Roadshow Gets Under Way
items.body: The AI company is marketing its Nasdaq listing under the ticker 'ANT', with about a fifth of the shares reported to be set aside for retail investors. Pricing is expected on 18 November.

items.headline: Polymarket Cuts Staff Ahead of Possible Listing
items.body: The prediction market confirmed company-wide layoffs, mostly of contractors, alongside leadership changes as it prepares for a potential 2027 IPO. It is reportedly finalising a $1 billion round at about a $21 billion valuation.

items.headline: Tata Power's Profit Jumps in Q2
items.body: The utility's consolidated September-quarter profit rose sharply on 26% revenue growth. Among smaller consumer names, condom maker Cupid more than doubled both profit and revenue.

items.headline: Monthly SIP Inflows Dip Slightly
items.body: Systematic investment plan contributions to Indian mutual funds eased from ₹32,490 Cr in September, while JSW Steel's October crude steel output rose 19% to 25.73 lakh tonnes.
